content.text:
The image shows an approved enemy sprite from the NES game Mega Man 2 (Capcom), enlarged: each square block is
ONE pixel, and the sprite is 28 x 29 pixels.

The enemy: A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes.

Draw the SECOND frame of its swim animation: the stroke pose: the tentacles flare out wide (spread apart, tips curling outward) as it pushes; the mantle and eyes stay the same, at most 1 pixel higher.

Hard rules:
- It must be the SAME sprite: same character, same colours, same outline, same eyes and face, same pixel size
  (each pixel the same enlarged square block as in the input), about the same 28 x 29
  pixel footprint, same position on the canvas. Change ONLY what the motion needs.
- Real NES pixel art: clean square pixel blocks, no anti-aliasing, gradients, blur or new colours.
- The sprite alone on the same plain flat grey-blue background. No text, no frame, no second sprite.

General guidance:
- Frames of a motion are complementary. When only two frames show a motion, make them its two extremes, with the
most contrast between them. Motion has a direction relative to the way the character faces: if one pose reaches up
and forward, its partner tends down and back (a crouch before a jump leans back when the jump goes up and
forward). Do not make a pose symmetric unless the motion itself is symmetric.
- Before drawing a frame, decide which parts of the body move in this motion and how each one moves (in a typical
run, the legs swing one way, the arms the other, the body rotates in a complementary way, and the head stays still).
Parts that do not move must not change at all: the same pixels in the same place. This matters most for outlines
(keep exactly the same line weight) and for expressive parts like the eyes.
